chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام:
Regarding the prayer of the advancing troops, he said:
“You pronounce the takbīr and the tahlīl.
Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ‘But if you fear, then on foot or while riding.’

key_terms.الزَّحْفِ: the advancing of troops or battle movement
key_terms.تُكَبِّرُ: you say the takbir, proclaiming Allahu Akbar
key_terms.تُهَلِّلُ: you say the tahlil, proclaiming La ilaha illa Allah
key_terms.خِفْتُمْ: you fear, meaning a state of danger or threat
key_terms.رُكْبَانًا: while riding, mounted in travel or combat
key_terms.رِجَالًا: on foot, while walking or standing
key_terms.صَلَاةِ: salat (prayer), specifically the ritual prayer under discussion

ai.seo_question: How is salat performed during fear or battle in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a ruling for salat in a state of intense fear during military advance or combat. It indicates that in such circumstances the prayer is reduced to takbir and tahlil, supported by the Qur'anic allowance to pray while on foot or riding.
